cells.title: Let the same worker re-claim a cell after unclaim (issue 154)
cells.action: GitHub issue 154. Repro: claim a cell with worker W through `dispatch prepare --claim` (it reserves the cell's files), run `bee cells unclaim --id <cell>`, then run the same `dispatch prepare --claim` again with the same worker W: it refuses with `reservation conflict ... - W holds <path> (cell <cell>)` — a conflict on its own hold. Cause: reserve_exec in verbs/reservations/reserve.rs excludes the same agent from find_conflicts, but the O_EXCL lease create then meets the agent's own live lease and reports it as a conflict; unclaim_cell in verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs never releases the cell's reservations. Contract (decision 7d3c57e8): (1) reserving a path that already carries a live lease of the SAME agent for the SAME cell succeeds (ok true; refresh the lease expiry) instead of conflicting; a different agent or a different cell still conflicts exactly as before. (2) `bee cells unclaim` releases the reservations held for that cell (all agents' leases whose cell is that id), fail-open on release errors after the status flip. Write the red test first for each point (watch it fail for the reported reason), then fix. The prepare.rs unwind ladder stays as is.

cells.title: Merge a worktree when main has a dirty bee store (issue 155)
cells.action: GitHub issue 155. Repro: main has uncommitted changes under .bee/ (for example .bee/backlog.jsonl modified and a new .bee/cells/<id>.json) and the feature branch also changes those store files; `bee worktree merge --id <wt> --json` fails with WORKTREE_MERGE_ABORT_FAILED: `git merge --no-ff --no-commit wt/<feature>` refuses with 'Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge' and the status shows the store files STAGED (`M  .bee/backlog.jsonl`, `A  .bee/cells/...`). Suspected cause: the merge stages the store into the index but the bookkeeping commit does not commit those staged files before git merge runs. Find the staging and bookkeeping_commit path under verbs/worktree/ (phases.rs and its siblings; the file list is a guess, touch only the worktree module), reproduce it in a test against a real temp git repo first and watch it fail for the reported reason, then fix. Contract (decision 51fe42f6): with a dirty .bee store on main, `bee worktree merge` succeeds — the store changes are committed in the bookkeeping commit (or otherwise never left staged in the index) before git merge starts; a merge that fails for another reason still restores main as found; no non-store dirty file is ever swept into a commit.

cells.title: Vendor the bee binary with its prompts on onboard (issue 156)
cells.action: GitHub issue 156. Repro: a host has .bee/bin/bee at an older version (2.67.0); running a newer bee `onboard --repo-root <host> --apply` from the beehive source rewrites .bee/bin/prompts/* to the new templates but leaves .bee/bin/bee old, so every `bee dispatch prepare` in the host refuses with 'prompt skew — .bee/bin/prompts/worker-cell.md does not match the worker-cell template compiled into this binary'. Cause: onboard/plan.rs plans copy_prompt but nothing for .bee/bin/bee. Contract (decision 2b906517): onboard plans a new item (for example `copy_binary`, path `.bee/bin/bee` or `.bee/bin/bee.exe` on Windows) when the host's vendored binary is missing-but-hooks-expect-it or its bytes differ from the running binary (std::env::current_exe), and apply copies it atomically (temp file in the same dir, then rename, keep the executable mode). It must never plan or write when the running binary IS the target file (same canonical path or same bytes — self-onboard of the beehive checkout, and a worktree whose .bee/bin/bee is a symlink into another checkout; see the current_exe warning in onboard/source.rs). The item shows in the dry-run plan like every other item. Write red tests first (plan item present for a stale host binary; absent when bytes match; absent when target is the running file), then fix. Keep current_exe injectable for tests.

truths: onboard apply leaves .bee/bin/bee and .bee/bin/prompts from one build
onboard never rewrites the binary when the source is the same file
the binary copy shows in the dry-run plan
key_links: the prompt-skew guard in verbs/drivers/prompt.rs compares vendored prompts to the binary's compiled templates
prohibitions: Do not replace a binary through a symlink into another checkout

cells.title: Render the deployment brief for native deploy dispatches (issue 157)
cells.action: GitHub issue 157. Repro: with team.claude.deploy on a native model (sonnet), `bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind gather --role deploy --stage deployment --feature <f> --release-version 2.73.0 --json` returns an Agent payload whose prompt says 'Gather: ... Read-only — never write ...' and carries no BEE_DISPATCH_ID, while the herding shape renders the 'Deploy-stage execution brief' with the id exported. Cause in verbs/drivers/prepare.rs: pane_prompt uses deployment_prompt(ver) only for the herding/cli arms; the claude Agent arm, the codex arms and the escalated arm use prompt_body; the BEE_DISPATCH_ID / BEE_RELEASE_VERSION / BEE_SESSION_ID export is added only to a `command` payload. Contract (decision 93ec1728): on a deployment-stage dispatch every transport carries the deployment brief; a payload with no `command` (Agent, spawn_agent) carries the brief plus explicit lines naming the dispatch id, release version and issuer session and telling the worker to export BEE_DISPATCH_ID, BEE_RELEASE_VERSION and BEE_SESSION_ID on the shell that runs scripts/release.sh; the Agent payload names a write-capable bee agent type (never bee-gather, which has no Bash), and the model-guard hook must accept that payload (check hooks/model_guard.rs; if it needs a change, report [BLOCKED] naming it rather than editing outside your files). Herding and cli payloads stay byte-identical. Write red tests first (Agent payload prompt has the deploy brief and dispatch id; agent type is not bee-gather; herding payload unchanged), then fix.

truths: a native deploy-stage Agent payload carries the deployment brief and the dispatch id
the native deploy payload names a write-capable agent type
herding and cli deploy payloads stay byte-identical
key_links: scripts/release.sh runs bee dispatch authorize with BEE_DISPATCH_ID
